flawed_step: The tournament hypothesis alone does not imply the existence of a Hamiltonian cycle.
counterexample: Let the vertices be {1,2,3,4}, with arc i→j exactly when i<j. Thus the arcs are 1→2, 1→3, 1→4, 2→3, 2→4, and 3→4. This is a tournament on exactly four vertices. Every directed edge increases the vertex label, so it contains no directed cycle at all, and therefore no Hamiltonian cycle.
assessment_summary: The transitive tournament on four vertices satisfies every hypothesis but violates the conclusion.
